name: Road Endpoints
purpose: A road built straight from cluster points ends on the Vtx its polygon sits on, which puts its last stretch inside the intersection.

name: Road Orientation
purpose: A lane profile is directional.

name: Roads and Polygons
purpose: The node never asks you where the intersections go.

name: Socket Actor
purpose: A marker you place to give a level entry or an actor entry a named socket.
situation: A level or actor kit piece needs known attachment points, so whatever places it can hang props, joins or decals off them.

name: Apply Sampling Details
purpose: A sampler normally writes what it found to attributes and leaves the point where it is.
situation: Points that should snap onto whatever they sampled, in some axes but not others, without a separate transform node downstream.

name: Attachment Rules
purpose: How a spawned component sits under the actor that owns it.
situation: Components being spawned onto an actor whose own transform should partly apply and partly not.

name: Attribute Gather Details
purpose: Which attributes a node should pick up, named by pattern rather than one at a time.
situation: A node acting on a set of attributes that is not known when the graph is authored.

name: Attribute To Tag Details
purpose: Turns attribute values into tags on the data.
situation: A value that has to survive as something the graph can branch on, rather than as data a later node has to read.

name: Blending Details
purpose: How several values become one.
situation: A node that combines several elements into one, on data whose attributes should not all be treated the same way.

name: Cell Artifacts Details
purpose: The Artifacts block, carried by every cell node, deciding what a cell that survived the constraints turns into on the way out.
situation: A cell node has found the regions you wanted and the remaining question is what shape they should arrive in, and which of each cell's own measurements should travel with them.

name: Cell Constraints Details
purpose: The Constraints block, and where most cell settings live.
situation: A cell node is handing back loops that were never wanted, and the ones that were can be told apart by something they measure.

name: Cell Growth Details
purpose: The Growth block: how far a claim spreads out from the cell a seed or a hole point landed in, counted in cells.
situation: A seed should come away with a territory rather than a single region, or a hole should clear the ring of regions around it.

name: Cell Seed Mutation Details
purpose: The Seed Mutations block, carried by Pathfinding : Find Cells and Pathfinding : Find Cells (Bounded).
situation: The found regions are wanted as one point each rather than as paths, or something downstream needs a point per region carrying that region's size.

name: Collision Details
purpose: What counts as geometry, for the nodes that query the physics world.
situation: A node reading the level's collision, where the wrong surfaces are being found or none are.

name: Connector Constraints
purpose: Attachment is exact: two connector frames mate and the child lands in precisely one place.
situation: Reading how the constraint list runs, before reading what any one constraint does.

name: Connector : Angular Range
purpose: Rotates the child around a frame axis in evenly-spaced steps across an angular range.
situation: Several placements around one socket, all at the same distance.

name: Connector : Arc Repeat
purpose: Places evenly-spaced variants along an arc at a radius, each rotated to follow the curve.
situation: Pieces laid around a circle, facing the way the circle runs: a colonnade, a ring of buildings.

name: Connector : Arc Surface
purpose: Slides the attachment point to a random spot in an arc-shaped area of the frame plane.
situation: Scatter that should respect a round boundary rather than a rectangular one.

name: Connector : Branch
purpose: Forks the variant pool on a condition, runs a separate sub-pipeline over each side, and rejoins them.
situation: One socket where some candidates need one treatment and the rest need another.

name: Connector : Conic Range
purpose: Spreads variants over a cone surface rather than around a circle.
situation: A spray rather than a fan: branches leaving a trunk, spokes off a hub in three dimensions.

name: Connector : Context Condition
purpose: Tests a growth context property against a threshold and prunes the whole variant pool when it fails.
situation: A socket that should only participate for part of a run.

name: Connector : Hemisphere Offset
purpose: A random offset inside a dome facing along the frame forward axis.
situation: Scatter off a face that must not push pieces back through it.

name: Connector : Lattice
purpose: A two-dimensional grid of variants across the frame right and up plane.
situation: One socket that should produce a field of pieces rather than a few.

name: Connector : Look At
purpose: Re-orients each variant so a chosen local axis aims at, or away from, a target.
situation: Pieces that should point at something rather than inherit the orientation the attachment gave them.

name: Connector : Preset
purpose: Expands a Constraint Preset asset inline.
situation: The same constraint pipeline wanted on more than one connector.

name: Connector : Probability
purpose: Randomly rejects a fraction of the variants.
situation: A pattern that should read as partly filled rather than complete.

name: Connector : Scale Ramp
purpose: Scales the placement by a value read from the growth context, mapping a source range onto a scale range.
situation: Structure that should taper, or grow, with how far along the run it is.

name: Connector : Snap to Grid
purpose: Quantizes the attachment point onto a grid anchored at the frame origin.
situation: Variation that should still line up, so pieces read as placed rather than as dropped.

name: Connector : Spiral
purpose: A helix: rotation around the frame plus a progressive offset along its forward axis, with each variant turned to follow the curve.
situation: Anything that turns while it rises: stairs, ramps, a vine on a column.

name: Connector : Surface Offset
purpose: Slides the attachment point to a random spot in a rectangle on the frame right and up plane.
situation: Attachment that should vary across a face rather than land on one exact point.

name: Connector : Volume Offset
purpose: A random offset inside a box around the frame origin, oriented in frame space.
situation: Scatter that should have depth: foliage, debris, anything sitting off a surface rather than on it.

name: Working Frame
purpose: Every constraint resolves in a frame, and this is where that frame comes from.
situation: A pattern that comes out correct but oriented or centred somewhere other than intended.

name: Dot Comparison Details
purpose: The block that decides how closely two directions have to agree.
situation: A node has a direction to weigh against a reference, and the only thing left to say is how far apart the two are allowed to be.

name: Edge Direction Settings
purpose: An edge joins two Vtx and has no direction of its own, so any node that needs one has to pick an endpoint to call first.
situation: Edge directions came out pointing the opposite way from what the graph downstream expects, or half of them point one way and half the other.

name: Edge/Edge Intersections
purpose: Where two edges cross, and whether that crossing should become a point.
situation: A cluster whose edges cross each other, where the crossings should become junctions rather than being ignored.

name: Filter Result Details
purpose: The block a filter consumer shows when it records verdicts onto elements instead of acting on them.
situation: A downstream node needs to know which elements passed, and splitting the data in two would break the pairing or the ordering the rest of the graph depends on.

name: Flood Fill Edge Direction Details
purpose: A spread across a cluster gives every connection it crossed a natural direction, the way it travelled, and this block records that as a vector on the edges.
situation: The cluster needs to carry which way a fill ran, so a later node can orient meshes, drive tangents, or tell upstream connections from downstream ones.

name: Projection Details
purpose: The plane a node works on when it works in two dimensions.
situation: Any node that has to reduce three dimensions to two, and needs telling which two.

name: Geo Mesh Import Details
purpose: A mesh turned into a cluster arrives as bare positions and connections, and this block is what else comes with it.
situation: The cluster from a mesh needs to keep something the mesh knew, a paint layer or a UV set, so a later node can read it back off the vertices.

name: Bias : Affinity
purpose: Prefers modules that get on with their parent, read from Affinity Map assets.
situation: A library where some pieces belong beside each other and some do not, and saying so once beats writing it into every rule.

name: Bias : Attribute Driven
purpose: Scales one tagged family of candidates along growth depth, over a band you name.
situation: One category of module belongs at a particular depth band and nowhere else.

name: Bias : Connector Identifier
purpose: Reweights by connector identifier, the per-module socket name.
situation: A naming convention already exists on the sockets and should drive where growth expands.

name: Bias : Connector Priority
purpose: Reads the priority authored on the connector itself and turns it into a preference.
situation: Connector priorities are already authored and should shape a grammar as well as a plain growth.

name: Bias : Connector Type Preference
purpose: Reweights candidates by the type of the connector they would grow from, so a run can be steered to expand along one kind of socket before another.
situation: A structure that should follow one kind of connection first, corridors before doors, beams before panels.

name: Bias : Cooldown
purpose: Penalises whatever was picked recently, for a number of steps.
situation: A run producing visible runs of one module, where spacing them out is all that is wanted.

name: Bias : Depth Preference
purpose: Weights candidates by how many attachments separate the connector they would grow from its seed.
situation: A silhouette that should be compact or reaching, expressed as a preference rather than as a hard depth cap.

name: Bias : Distance Preference
purpose: The metric sibling of Bias : Depth Preference.
situation: A library of mixed-size pieces where counting attachments no longer describes how far the run has got.

name: Bias : Pity Counter
purpose: Boosts matching candidates the longer they go unpicked, and resets a candidate the moment it is chosen.
situation: A library where some pieces keep losing the draw and the result reads repetitive because of it.

name: Bias : Quota
purpose: Nudges the run toward a target proportion of placements matching a predicate.
situation: A ratio that should hold across a region, where being close is good enough.

name: Bias : Spatial
purpose: The soft form of Constraint : Spatial.
situation: Growth that should prefer a region without being forbidden from leaving it.

name: Bias : Tag Weight
purpose: The plainest bias in the set: a flat multiplier on candidates matching a tag predicate, with everything else left neutral.
situation: Prefer or suppress a category, by however much, with nothing conditional about it.

name: Bias : Target Proximity
purpose: Steers a run toward live target connectors: nearer scores higher, and optionally facing them counts too.
situation: Growth that should find its way to something rather than be confined while doing so.

name: Bias : Tensor Alignment
purpose: Reweights candidates by how well their connector aligns with a tensor field.
situation: One field, and parts of the grammar that should obey it more than others.

name: Bias Settings
purpose: What every grammar bias carries on top of the shared rule settings.
situation: Tuning how hard a bias leans without rewriting what it prefers.

name: Constraint : Claim Facts
purpose: Refuses candidates by the claim state of the parent module connectors: how many of its sockets are already spent, and which ones.
situation: A placement that should depend on how much of its parent is already used up.

name: Constraint : Count
purpose: Bounds how many placements in the active scope match a tag predicate, from below, from above, or both.
situation: A count that has to come out right rather than merely be likely.

name: Constraint : Depends On
purpose: Orders two kinds of placement without ordering the graph.
situation: One thing has to exist before another may be placed, and the grammar is not the natural place to say so.

name: Constraint : Forbid Pair
purpose: Mutual exclusion between two kinds of module.
situation: Two things that must not appear together, where either could plausibly be placed first.

name: Constraint : Once
purpose: Lets one specific module appear at most once in the active scope.
situation: Exactly one of a named module, and no way to express that as a tag.

name: Constraint : Orbital Facts
purpose: Refuses candidates by an orbital fact of either the parent module or the candidate itself.
situation: A placement that should depend on the orbital shape of what it is attaching to.

name: Constraint : Reach
purpose: A corridor constraint.
situation: Growth that has somewhere to be, and should not spread away from the route while getting there.

name: Constraint : Spatial
purpose: The keep-in and keep-out rule, scoped to whatever node or region hosts it.
situation: A region of the grammar that must build inside, or outside, a space you supplied.

name: Constraint : Unique
purpose: Once anything matching the predicate is placed in the active scope, later matches are refused.
situation: One boss room per floor, one entrance per building, one of a kind rather than one named thing.

name: Constraint Settings
purpose: What every grammar constraint carries on top of the shared rule settings: when it is consulted, and what happens when it refuses.
situation: Deciding when a constraint should be asked, and how hard its failure should hit.

name: Corridor
purpose: The target-seeking behaviour Seek and Route share.
situation: Tuning how a corridor picks its target and what an unfinished one leaves behind.

name: Begin Region
purpose: Opens a span of grammar that a set of rules applies to.
situation: A rule that should apply to a stretch of the grammar rather than to one node.

name: Branch
purpose: Runs every child, in parallel, from the same parent.
situation: Several things that should grow from one place at once.

name: Join
purpose: Connects frontier connectors across branches with a spanning module.
situation: Two parts of a structure that should be joined because the design says so rather than because they happened to meet.

name: Choice
purpose: Picks one child at random, by weight, and runs only that one.
situation: One of several continuations, chosen rather than combined.

name: End Region
purpose: Closes the nearest open region of the same name.
situation: A region whose rules should stop applying partway through.

name: Fill
purpose: Grows until the frontier is exhausted rather than until a count is reached.
situation: A space that should be filled out rather than a run of a given length.

name: Filter
purpose: Narrows the frontier without placing anything.
situation: A section of grammar that should only work on part of what is available.

name: Graph Input
purpose: The source-side boundary of a subgraph.
situation: A grammar meant to be referenced, that needs an entry point other than a Seed.

name: Graph Output
purpose: The sink-side boundary of a subgraph.
situation: A reusable grammar fragment that has to hand its frontier back to its caller.

name: Growth
purpose: Runs a small growth loop inside one node, placing several modules from the frontier rather than one.
situation: A run of modules where the count is a range rather than a number.

name: Merge
purpose: Fan-in.
situation: Work that should only start once everything before it is done.

name: Module
purpose: Places one module matching its descriptor.
situation: One module, at one place, chosen by what it has to satisfy rather than by name.

name: Optional
purpose: Runs its body, or does not, on a probability roll.
situation: A step that should happen sometimes.

name: Module Descriptor
purpose: What a placing node asks the library for.
situation: Deciding what a placement node is allowed to draw from.

name: Prune
purpose: Removes placed modules that led nowhere and hands their sockets back to the frontier.
situation: A run that produces stubs, corridors to nowhere, or branches that stopped one module in.

name: Repeat
purpose: Runs its body a number of times drawn between two bounds.
situation: A structure that should continue for a while rather than a fixed number of steps.

name: Route
purpose: Solves an exact corridor to a target before committing any of it.
situation: A connection that has to land exactly, where a corridor that stops short is worse than no corridor.

name: Seed
purpose: The only entry point a grammar has.
situation: Every grammar. There is no graph without one.

name: Seek
purpose: Grows a corridor toward a live target and joins when it comes in range.
situation: A route to somewhere, where getting there matters more than the corridor being optimal.

name: Sequence
purpose: Runs its children in order, handing each one what the last produced.
situation: Steps that have to happen in a fixed order.

name: Multi Spawn
purpose: Whether one connector may host more than one child.
situation: A socket authored to take several children, on a node that should fill it.

name: Subgraph
purpose: Runs another grammar inline.
situation: A section of grammar wanted in more than one place, or a graph grown too large to read.

name: Yield
purpose: A sink inside a Repeat body.
situation: A repeated body where each pass should continue from the last.

name: Rule Settings
purpose: The settings every grammar rule carries, biases and constraints alike, so they are documented once here rather than on each of the twenty-three.
situation: Reading what the fields above a rule own settings do, whichever rule you are looking at.

name: Graph Builder Details
purpose: The step between a node finishing its connections and a cluster arriving on the pins, labelled Cluster Output Settings wherever it appears.
situation: A generator produced more islands than wanted, or its edge points came out as bare dots when they were expected to look like the connections they stand for.

name: Influence Details
purpose: How much of an effect actually lands.
situation: An operation whose full effect is too strong, or which should apply to some points and not others.

name: Justification Details
purpose: Where a fitted thing sits inside the space it was fitted to.
situation: Assets fitted into bounds that do not match their proportions, where the leftover room should go somewhere specific.

name: Manhattan Details
purpose: Turns a straight line between two points into a staircase of axis-aligned steps.
situation: Connections that should look like corridors, pipework or circuitry rather than direct lines.

name: Matching Details
purpose: The block a node embeds to accept match rules.
situation: A node showing a Mode dropdown and a Match Rules pin, and the question of what the settings under it do once rules are attached.

name: Node Selection Details
purpose: Seeds and goals are ordinary points that know nothing about the cluster they aim at, so something has to turn each of them into a Vtx to start from or end at.
situation: A pathfinding node came back with fewer paths than there were seeds, or a fill started from a vertex on the wrong side of the cluster.

name: Path/Edge Intersections
purpose: Where a path crosses an edge, and whether that crossing should become a point on it.
situation: Paths crossing a cluster's edges, where the crossings should become points rather than being passed through.

name: Paths Output Settings
purpose: A size gate on paths a node invents rather than receives, shown in the panel as Paths Output Settings.
situation: A pathfinding run came back with as many single-hop paths as real routes, and only the longer ones are wanted.

name: Path Statistics
purpose: The block behind Visited output mode.
situation: A batch of queries is being run to find out which parts of a network carry traffic, and the routes themselves are of no interest.

name: Property Output Settings
purpose: The shared answer to which declared properties get written out, and under what attribute names.
situation: A schema declares more than this graph wants on its points, or one of its properties needs a different attribute name here than everywhere else.

name: Selector Base Config
purpose: The concerns every selector carries beside its own picking strategy.
situation: Two selectors reading the same points keep producing the same picks, or picks need restricting to a slice of the collection by name.

name: Socket Output Details
purpose: One shared block for turning sockets into points, carried by the nodes that emit a Sockets pin.
situation: An asset carries more sockets than the graph wants, or the socket points need to say which socket and which asset they came from.

name: Tensor Sampling Settings
purpose: Everything the node reading a field does to the answer once the tensors have finished with it.
situation: An extrusion is stepping too far or barely moving, or a field is wanted for its direction alone and its magnitude keeps getting into the result.

name: Tensor Sampling Mutations Details
purpose: The last thing one tensor does to its own answer before that answer joins the field.
situation: A field that is right in plan and wrong in elevation, or one tensor in a stack that has to push the other way from the rest of them.

name: Topology Details
purpose: Everything the topology nodes decide about the mesh once its triangles exist.
situation: A surface that triangulated correctly and still needs shading, coordinates and normals before anything can render it.

name: UVW
purpose: A position inside a point's bounds, named as a fraction rather than a distance.
situation: Naming a spot on or inside a point's bounds that should mean the same thing whatever the point's size.

name: Filter Sources
purpose: The block every Valency point filter opens with, and the question all four have to answer before they can test anything: where does the Valency Map come from.
situation: Wiring any of the Valency filters, whatever it is testing.

name: Get Collection Member
purpose: Reads any authorable field of the collection asset itself into a Blueprint graph, addressed by name.
situation: A staging pipeline or editor utility needs a value that lives on the collection rather than on one of its rows.

name: Get Entry Member
purpose: Reads any authorable field of one collection entry into a Blueprint graph, addressed by raw index and field name.
situation: A pipeline hook has an entry index in hand and needs that row's authored value before deciding what to write back.

name: Get Entry Property
purpose: Reads a declared property of one entry, resolved the way the rest of the collection system resolves it.
situation: A pipeline or editor utility needs the value a given entry resolves for a declared property, without caring which tier supplies it.

name: Set Collection Member
purpose: Writes one reflected member of the collection asset itself from Blueprint.
situation: A staging pipeline or editor utility needs to set a collection-wide value, the same edit an author would make in the collection's details panel, without opening every collection by hand.

name: Set Entry Member
purpose: Writes one reflected member of a single collection entry, addressed by its raw index.
situation: A staging pipeline hook holds an entry index and needs to write a field of that entry, the same edit an author would make in the collection's grid.

name: Set Entry Property
purpose: Writes one of the collection's declared properties onto a single entry, addressed by its raw index, and enables that entry's own override for it.
situation: A staging pipeline computes a per-entry value and needs it stored as that entry's own override rather than left to the collection default.

name: Switch on Collection Type
purpose: Branches Blueprint execution on which kind of collection it was handed, and hands that collection back already cast.
situation: One staging pipeline is assigned to collections of several types and needs a different branch per type.

name: Action : Abstract
purpose: The shape every action shares, and the page to read once rather than on each of them.
situation: Reading the settings any action node shares before going to the specific one that does the work.

name: Action : Write Attributes
purpose: Stamps one set of attribute values onto the points that pass its conditions and a different set onto the points that fail.
situation: Marking points with a small block of typed values according to a test, where the values are authored once as an attribute set rather than repeated per node.

name: Collection | Actor
purpose: A weighted list of actor classes for staging to pick from.
situation: A handful of actors were dressed by hand in a level, and they now have to become a pickable library that spawns them configured the same way.

name: State : Bitmask Adjacency
purpose: A state whose bits are keyed to directions.
situation: A cluster on a layout with a known set of directions, where what matters about a Vtx is which of them it has an edge in.

name: Affinity Map
purpose: How strongly given modules prefer each other, expressed as predicate pairs with a weight.
situation: A library where some pieces belong beside each other and saying so once beats writing it into every rule.

name: Filter : Angle
purpose: Tests the corner an ordered element makes with the element before it and the element after it.
situation: An ordered point set where what survives depends on how sharply the run turns at each element.

name: Asset Collection
purpose: The abstract base every collection type inherits, and the page for the settings that are identical on every one of them.
situation: Reading any collection type's page and needing to know what its Collection Properties, Category Overrides, Global rules or Subcollection Bounds Mode do, since those are the same on all of them.

name: Staging : Distribute
purpose: This is where a point gets its entry.
situation: Points exist and something has to decide what each of them becomes, or an earlier decision has to be partly rolled again without disturbing the rest.

name: Data Filter : Attribute Exists
purpose: Asks whether a dataset declares an attribute of a given name, and answers for the dataset as a whole.
situation: Datasets arriving from several branches, where the work downstream needs an attribute only some of them were built with.

name: Attribute Hash
purpose: Reduces one attribute's values, across a whole dataset, to a single integer that identifies them.
situation: Several datasets have to be told apart, or matched up, by what one of their attributes holds.

name: Attribute Remap
purpose: Rescales one numeric attribute or point property into a different range, with the input range taken from the data rather than guessed.
situation: A value with an unknown spread has to become a 0 to 1 weight, or a driver whose response should not be linear.

name: Path : Attribute Rolling
purpose: Walks a path from one end to the other carrying a state, and writes down what that state was at every point.
situation: A path that has to be cut into named stretches by a condition on its points, whether or not anything is blended along them.

name: Attribute Stats
purpose: Measures every attribute on the input and reports what it found: extremes, average, how many distinct values there are, how many occur exactly once, and how many points never moved off the attribute's default.
situation: A value is behaving strangely and you need to know its real spread, or a graph has to branch on whether an attribute was ever written to.

name: Promote Attributes
purpose: Lifts a value off one row of a dataset and attaches it to the dataset as a whole.
situation: A per-element value that later nodes need to match, sort or branch on at the dataset level, where reading it per element is the wrong granularity.

name: Auto
purpose: Splits the tangent length between arrive and leave according to where the point sits between its two neighbours.
situation: Points along the path are unevenly spaced and a curve built from equal-length tangents swings wide over the short gaps.

name: Batch Actions
purpose: Runs a stack of Action sub-nodes over one set of points, so several filter-driven writes happen in one pass instead of one node each.
situation: Several independent per-point tests that each need to write something, where splitting and re-merging the points once per test would be the alternative.

name: Path : Bevel
purpose: Cuts a corner off and puts a profile in its place.
situation: A path of hard corners that has to read as rounded, or as chamfered, before anything is built along it.

name: Cluster : BFS Depth
purpose: Answers how far every Vtx sits from the nearest seed, counted in edges crossed.
situation: Seed points sit somewhere on or near a cluster, and everything downstream needs to know how many steps away each Vtx is.

name: Bin Packing 3D (Q4RealBPP)
purpose: Packs items into bins under the constraints real loading has: weight limits, things that must not sit on each other, and nothing left floating in mid-air.
situation: Crates, props or cargo that should stack the way real ones would, with heavy things low and nothing hovering.

name: Bin Packing
purpose: Fits points into containers by moving them, so that their bounds stop overlapping and stay inside the bin.
situation: Objects of assorted sizes that have to be arranged inside authored volumes without intersecting.

name: Bitmask Collection
purpose: A named vocabulary of bit patterns, held in one asset instead of typed into every node.
situation: Several graphs that have to agree on what a given bit means, where the meaning is still moving.

name: Filter : Bitmask
purpose: Reads a 64-bit integer attribute as a set of flags and asks how it stands against a mask: whether the two share any bit, whether the flags carry every bit of the mask, whether they are identical, or the negations of the first two.
situation: Several boolean states are packed into one integer attribute, and the next node should act only on the elements carrying a particular combination of them.

name: Bitmask Merge
purpose: Folds several masks arriving on one pin into a single mask.
situation: A mask assembled from parts that different branches of the graph decide independently.

name: Bitmask
purpose: Builds one 64-bit mask in the graph and hands it out as data.
situation: A mask that more than one node has to agree on, or one that a graph parameter needs to be able to override.

name: Bitmask Operation
purpose: Applies one bitwise operation to an int64 attribute on every point.
situation: A flag attribute that needs a bit added, cleared or flipped after the pass that created it.

name: Uber Blend
purpose: Blending with no second dataset and no geometry involved: a point's attributes against each other, in place.
situation: An attribute needs to become some expression of the other attributes on the same point.

name: Blend Op Factory
purpose: The object a Blend Ops pin actually carries, and the contract every consumer of that pin reads it through.
situation: Working out why a mix of BlendOp and BlendOp : Blend All nodes on one pin produced fewer operations than nodes wired, or why one of them had no effect.

name: BlendOp
purpose: One attribute, one blend mode, one destination.
situation: A node offers blending and only one attribute should move, on terms you want to state exactly.

name: BlendOp : Blend All
purpose: The other half of the Blend Ops pin: instead of naming one attribute, it takes everything the data carries and gives it all the same treatment.
situation: Everything on the points should carry across a blend, with two or three exceptions.

name: Path : Blend
purpose: Rewrites every point of a path from its own two ends.
situation: A run whose values have to ramp from one end to the other, where the two ends are already carrying what the ramp should start and finish at.

name: Filter : Bool Compare
purpose: Tests a boolean read on the element against a second one, either a typed true or false or another attribute on that same element.
situation: A flag already written onto the elements, and the next node should act only where it is set.

name: Bounds Axis To Points
purpose: Picks one axis of each point's bounds and produces the pair of points at its ends.
situation: Boxes of varying proportion and orientation that each need to yield a spanning segment, chosen by a rule rather than by hand.

name: Filter : Inclusion (Bounds)
purpose: Tests each element against the bounds of other points.
situation: A second point set marks out regions through its point bounds, and an element survives by landing inside one of them.

name: Path × Bounds Intersection
purpose: Finds where a path passes through the volumes of a set of points and puts a point at each of those places.
situation: A path runs through a scattering of volumes and something has to happen exactly at the borders: a marker, a split later on, or a value taken from whichever volume was crossed.

name: Bounds To Points
purpose: Puts a new point somewhere on each existing point's bounds.
situation: Points that need a companion at their base, their top face, or a chosen corner, produced consistently across a set of varied sizes.

name: Box Fitting
purpose: The fitting rule that takes its collision shape from the points themselves.
situation: Vtx standing for something with a real footprint that the points' own bounds already describe, packed tightly enough that the footprints intersect.

name: Box Fitting v2
purpose: The fitting rule whose collision box you author instead of inherit.
situation: Vtx standing for footprints whose size lives in an attribute, or a cluster where the direction overlapping pairs move matters as much as the fact that they move.

name: Branch on Data
purpose: Routes whole datasets down named pins by reading one @Data value off each of them.
situation: Datasets that were stamped with a kind, a state or an enum value upstream, and now need to take different routes without being merged and re-split.

name: Cluster : Break to Paths
purpose: Reads a cluster back out as paths, so everything phrased in terms of order becomes available again: resampling, offsetting, sweeping a mesh along a run.
situation: A cluster has been generated and refined down to the connections that were meant, and the runs between its junctions now have to be treated as ordered geometry.

name: Build Asset Collection
purpose: Every other route into staging starts from a collection someone authored and saved.
situation: The list of assets to stage from is decided by the graph, from a data table or a filtered set of paths, so no saved collection can name it up front.

name: Cluster : Cell Diagram
purpose: Reads the closed cells of a cluster and hands back a second cluster made of them: one Vtx at the middle of each cell, joined to the cells it shares a side with.
situation: A layout of rooms, plots or districts exists as the closed cells of a cluster and the next step is about which of them touch.

name: Cluster : Convex Hull 2D
purpose: Finds the outer boundary of a point set as seen from one direction and gives it back in order, as a closed path and as a cluster ring.
situation: A scatter needs the outline that encloses it, as an ordered loop rather than as a set.

name: Cluster : Convex Hull 3D
purpose: Keeps the points that sit on the outside of a cloud and throws the rest away, wiring what survives into a cluster.
situation: A point cloud needs its outer shell isolated, either as a cage to build on or to get rid of everything buried inside it.

name: Cluster : Build Custom Graph
purpose: Builds a cluster from Blueprint rather than from a rule.
situation: Connectivity that already exists somewhere outside PCG and has to be reproduced rather than inferred.

name: Cluster : Delaunay 2D
purpose: Triangulates a point set as it looks from one direction, and hands back the same points as Vtx with connections between them.
situation: A scattered set of points needs connectivity across a surface, a ground plane or a facade rather than through the space between them.

name: Cluster : Delaunay 3D
purpose: Turns a loose point cloud into a dense cluster by tetrahedralising it: every point keeps its place and gains connections to the neighbours it shares a tetrahedron with.
situation: A scattered point cloud has to become a connected cluster and nothing in the data says which points belong together.

name: Cluster : Edge Dual Graph
purpose: Swaps the two halves of a cluster over: every connection becomes a Vtx, and the new connections join the ones that sat next to each other around a shared endpoint.
situation: A question is about the connections of a cluster rather than its vertices, and the tools available all work on vertices.

name: Cluster : Voronoi 2D
purpose: Reads the input points as cell seeds, viewed from one direction, and builds the cell walls between them: the Vtx are cell corners and the connections run along the boundaries.
situation: A set of seed positions has to become the walls, plots or districts that divide the space between them, with the seeds coming back as plot centres.

name: Cluster : Voronoi 3D
purpose: Reads the input points as cell seeds and builds the skeleton between the cells: the Vtx are the corners where cells meet, and each connection runs along a shared cell wall.
situation: A set of seed positions has to become the lattice of walls or struts that separates them, rather than a web joining them.

name: Catmull-Rom
purpose: Both vectors get half the straight-line vector from the previous point to the next, the uniform Catmull-Rom tangent.
situation: A path of reasonably even spacing is on its way to a spline and should read as one continuous curve, with no point treated as special.

name: Channel Map
purpose: Typed values on modules, under named channels: numbers, vectors, colours or names, assigned by tag predicate.
situation: A per-position value already exists and the modules should follow it.

name: Cherry Pick Points
purpose: Keeps the points a picker named and drops the rest.
situation: A dataset where the points to keep, or the points to remove, are known by their position rather than by anything they carry.

name: Clipper2 : Boolean
purpose: Combines closed shapes by area: keeping what they share, what either covers, what one covers and the other does not, or what exactly one of them covers.
situation: Two sets of closed outlines overlap and only the overlap, the merger, or the remainder is wanted, as real geometry rather than as a selection.

name: Clipper2 : Decompose
purpose: Cuts a closed footprint into convex cells and hands the result back as a cluster.
situation: A closed path outlines an area that has to be worked with as a set of convex cells rather than as one outline.

name: Clipper2 : Offset
purpose: Grows or shrinks a shape by a distance, solving the whole outline at once so corners round or square off cleanly and self-overlap is resolved rather than left folded.
situation: A footprint needs a border, an inset, or a nest of rings at even spacing, and the corners have to survive the operation.

name: Clipper2 Processor
purpose: The shared surface behind the nodes that hand their paths to the Clipper2 library.
situation: Several path datasets were wired into a Clipper2 node, and the question is whether they were solved as one shape or as several, and where the output points took their attributes from.

name: Clipper2 : Rect Clip
purpose: Cuts paths to a rectangle, taking that rectangle either from the bounds of whatever is wired to the operand pin or from a box typed into the panel.
situation: Paths have to be trimmed to a tile, a cell, or the extent of some other dataset, and the boundary is a box.

name: Clipper2 : Triangulate
purpose: Fills closed paths into a mesh, and unlike the other filling nodes it says what to do when the outlines overlap.
situation: Outlines with holes or overlaps, where which parts should be solid is a decision rather than an accident.

name: Clipper2 : Volume
purpose: Turns a closed path into a spawned actor with real collision matching its footprint, extruded upward.
situation: A region drawn as a path in the graph that has to exist in the level as something gameplay or rendering can query.

name: Cluster : Centrality
purpose: Scores every Vtx by how central it is to its cluster and writes the score as one double attribute.
situation: A cluster where the next operation has to treat junctions differently from dead ends, and the difference has to arrive as a number sitting on each Vtx.

name: Cluster : Decomposition
purpose: Splits a cluster's Vtx into groups and writes each Vtx's group as an integer CellID.
situation: One large cluster that has to be worked on in pieces, where the pieces are decided by a rule and carried as an attribute instead of by cutting the cluster apart.

name: Cluster : Diffuse
purpose: Spreads attribute values outward from seeds across a cluster and reconciles them where the spreads overlap.
situation: Several sources need to paint values across a cluster and their reaches have to meet in a graded boundary rather than a hard one.

name: Cluster : Flood Fill
purpose: Grows a spread outward from each seed until the fill controls stop it, then hands back what the spread learned.
situation: A branching structure has to be grown across a cluster from a handful of starting points, and both the reach and the lanes it took are wanted.

name: Cluster Filter Definition
purpose: The branch of the filter contract that is handed the cluster.
situation: Deciding whether a condition belongs on a Vtx Filters pin, on an Edge Filters pin, or on a plain point filter that would serve either.

name: Collection | Cluster Sketch
purpose: A collection whose entries are Cluster Sketch assets, so hand-authored clusters distribute with the same weighted machinery as any other staged asset.
situation: Hand-authored structural pieces have to be picked per point, weighted and categorized like a library of meshes.

name: Edges Processor Settings
purpose: The shared surface behind every node that takes a cluster on its own two pins, from Cluster : Refine to Pathfinding : Edges.
situation: A cluster node was handed several Vtx and Edges datasets at once, and the question is which of them it paired, which it dropped, and how many times it ran.

name: Cluster to Zone Graph
purpose: Turns a cluster into Zone Graph data the engine's navigation can use.
situation: A road, path or corridor network built as a cluster that now has to exist as navigable Zone Graph.

name: Collection Staging Pipeline
purpose: A staging pipeline is a Blueprint or C++ object attached to a collection, running your own logic every time its staging data is rebuilt in the editor.
situation: A convention a team would otherwise enforce by hand across every entry, naming-driven tags or a derived cost property, has to re-apply itself on every rebuild.

name: Collocation Count
purpose: Counts how many other points share each point's position.
situation: Data merged from several sources where the same location may have been produced more than once, and it matters how often.

name: Cluster : Connect
purpose: Joins the separate components of one cluster by inserting edges between them.
situation: A generator returned four islands where one navigable network was wanted, and they need joining at their nearest points.

name: Cluster : Connect Points
purpose: The open-ended generator: it holds no opinion about what should connect, and takes that decision from probe sub-nodes wired to its Probes pin.
situation: A scatter of points that has to become a cluster under a rule you choose, whether that rule is proximity, direction, index arithmetic or an attribute comparison.

name: Cluster : Connect Vtx
purpose: The second consumer of the probe family, and the one that starts from a cluster instead of a point cloud.
situation: Several clusters that have to be stitched into one, or a cluster that needs extra connections a probe rule can describe.

name: Enum Constant
purpose: Reads an enum, native or Blueprint, and hands its values to the graph as data.
situation: A graph that has to branch or match on the same enum a Blueprint or a C++ system uses, without the numbers being retyped and left to drift.

name: Filter : Constant
purpose: Answers the same way for every element, and reads nothing to do it.
situation: A consumer that has to pass or fail everything, either while the real condition is still being built or because something outside the graph decides it.

name: Constant
purpose: Emits fixed values as data, one output pin per value.
situation: A graph that needs pi, an axis or a plain 1 as data, with no field to fill in each time the node is placed.

name: Constraint Preset
purpose: A reusable bundle of connector constraints.
situation: The same constraint pipeline wanted in more than one place.

name: Copy Attributes
purpose: Moves attributes from one dataset onto another, one at a time or all at once, and it exists for the case the stock node stops short of: a @Data value copied onto per-element data reaches every element rather than only the first.
situation: A value that lives once per dataset has to become a per-point value, or attributes have to travel between two datasets that share nothing but their shape.

name: Cluster : Copy to Points
purpose: Puts a complete copy of each input cluster at every target point, moved onto that point's transform.
situation: One authored cluster, or a small library of them, has to appear across a scatter of points and be oriented to each.

name: Copy Tags
purpose: Copies data tags from reference Targets onto Sources, adding only the tags a Source does not already carry.
situation: Data that lost its tags through a node that does not preserve them, or that needs the tags of some other dataset it can be paired with.

name: Copy to Path
purpose: Bends a set of points along a path, the way a spline mesh bends a mesh.
situation: A block of points laid out in a straight line has to follow a curve, several curves, or the same curve at several places along it.

name: Copy to Points
purpose: Stamps a whole dataset onto every target point, sized and placed to fit.
situation: An authored arrangement of points that should appear at each of many targets, adapted to each target's size.

name: Heuristics : Attribute
purpose: Charges whatever a number on the cluster says to charge.
situation: The cost of crossing ground is already recorded on the cluster and a route needs to respect it.

name: Match : Attributes
purpose: Pairs data by comparing one value held on each side.
situation: Twenty inputs and twenty targets that already carry a shared id, and one node that has to work out the twenty pairs.

name: Match : By Index
purpose: Pairs data by position rather than by content.
situation: Two sets of the same length whose ordering already encodes the pairing, and no shared tag or id to express it with.

name: Match : Copy Tags
purpose: The rule that decides nothing.
situation: A pairing that is already expressed by other rules, and downstream nodes that need to know which target each input ended up with.

name: Match : Overlap
purpose: Pairs data by where it sits.
situation: Datasets tiled or scattered across a level, and an operation that should only pair the ones sharing space.

name: Match : Random
purpose: Thins a pairing out.
situation: Rules that pair correctly but pair too much, and a need for a repeatable subset rather than all of it.

name: Match : Shared Tag
purpose: Pairs data by the tags both sides already carry.
situation: Datasets tagged by whatever produced them, and a node that has to rebuild the pairing from those tags alone.

name: Match : Tags × Attributes
purpose: Pairs a tag on one side against an attribute on the other.
situation: Inputs tagged upstream by whatever produced them, and targets holding the same information as an attribute.

name: Shape : Circle
purpose: Builds a ring of points around each seed.
situation: Seeds that should each become a ring, an arc, or a fan of points around themselves.

name: Shape : φ Sphere
purpose: Builds points spread evenly over a sphere around each seed.
situation: Seeds that need points spread over a sphere without the crowding a latitude and longitude grid produces.

name: Shape : 3D Grid
purpose: Builds a lattice of points filling the space around each seed.
situation: Seeds that should each become a filled arrangement, for sampling a volume or scattering within a defined box.

name: Shape : Polygon
purpose: Builds a regular polygon around each seed, optionally with spokes running to its centre.
situation: Seeds that should become regular outlines, stars or wheels, with the corners identifiable afterwards.

name: Create Shapes
purpose: Runs the shape builders.
situation: Seed points that should each be replaced by a generated form, sized and oriented from the seed.

name: Create Spline
purpose: Turns each path into a spline.
situation: A run of points has to leave the graph as a spline, either as data for something that samples splines or as a component in the level.

name: Tensor : Constant
purpose: One authored direction, the same everywhere, with no source geometry and no pin to wire.
situation: An extrusion stops early in the empty spaces between effectors and the field needs a floor under it.

name: Tensor : Flow
purpose: Gives every effector point a heading and blends those headings into a current.
situation: A handful of oriented points have to stand in for wind, current or grain across an area.

name: Tensor : Inertia (Constant)
purpose: Hands back the heading the sampled thing already had, everywhere, with an optional twist applied to it.
situation: Extrusions should hold their heading across the whole field, or bend at a constant rate along it.

name: Tensor : Inertia
purpose: Hands back the heading the sampled thing already had.
situation: An extrusion crossing a patch of field should coast straight through it instead of being turned.

name: Tensor : Noise (Bounded)
purpose: The same noise reading as Tensor : Noise, confined to where effector points reach.
situation: A field should stay orderly except in a few marked pockets where it breaks up.

name: Tensor : Noise
purpose: Reads a 3D noise as a direction, at every position in the field.
situation: A flow reads too clean and needs wander added to it without moving any of the points that define it.

name: Tensor : Null
purpose: The eraser.
situation: A field is right everywhere except inside a few volumes where nothing should move.

name: Tensor : Path Flow
purpose: A current running along a curve, drawn from ordered points.
situation: Extrusions or transforms should follow a route that was already authored as a path.

name: Tensor : Path Pole
purpose: Pushes away from a curve drawn through ordered points.
situation: A route has to be kept clear, or things have to be gathered onto it.

name: Tensor : Pole
purpose: Turns effector points into a radial field.
situation: A handful of points mark where extrusions should be shoved aside, or gathered in.

name: Tensor : Spin
purpose: Turns effector points into vortices.
situation: Extrusions have to wind around a set of points rather than run at them or past them.

name: Tensor : Spline Flow
purpose: A current running along spline data.
situation: A spline actor already marks the route, and the field should follow it without turning it into points first.

name: Tensor : Spline Pole
purpose: Pushes away from spline data.
situation: A spline actor marks something to stay away from, or to be drawn onto.

name: Valency : Bias
purpose: Makes some modules likelier at some positions.
situation: A preference that varies across a cluster: taller pieces toward the perimeter, one family favoured on the ground floor.

name: Valency : Bias (Channel)
purpose: Biases by matching a value rather than by naming a tag.
situation: A per-position value already exists and the modules should follow it.

name: Cull On Empty
purpose: Stops a branch from running when there is nothing in it.
situation: A branch whose upstream sometimes produces nothing, where the downstream work is expensive or would write misleading empty results.

name: Cluster : Cut
purpose: Uses paths as cutting geometry against a cluster, removing whatever they run through.
situation: A road network or a set of boundary paths has to open a gap in a cluster that was generated without knowing about them.

name: Data Filter : Bounds
purpose: Measures the box a dataset occupies and compares one number taken from it, answering for the dataset as a whole.
situation: Several datasets on one pin where only the ones big enough, or square enough, deserve the expensive work downstream.

name: Data Hash
purpose: One random value derived from the shape of whatever is plugged in, and from nothing else.
situation: A whole branch of the graph needs one random value that stays the same until the upstream data meaningfully changes.

name: Filter : Data Match
purpose: Turns a dataset pairing into a filter verdict.
situation: Whole datasets have to be kept or dropped according to which reference dataset they belong with.

name: Flush Debug
purpose: Clears debug drawing from the viewport.
situation: A viewport cluttered with debug drawing from earlier runs or from nodes since disabled.

name: Decompose : BSP Occupancy
purpose: Drops the Vtx into a voxel grid and cuts that block of voxels in two with flat planes, again and again, preferring to cut through empty space.
situation: A cluster with visible voids in it, where the pieces should follow those voids instead of a uniform tiling.

name: Decompose : Convex BSP
purpose: Cuts the Vtx in half over and over until each piece is close enough to convex.
situation: Breaking a sprawling or bent cluster into pieces that each sit inside a tidy hull, for anything downstream that wants convex regions.

name: Decompose : Grid
purpose: The plainest of the seven.
situation: Cutting a cluster into even spatial tiles of a size you already know, where the tiling matters and the connectivity does not.

name: Decompose : Max Boxes
purpose: Carves the cluster into solid rectangles.
situation: Covering a cluster with rectangular regions, for anything downstream that wants boxes rather than arbitrary clumps.

name: Decompose : Max Boxes (Extended)
purpose: Decompose : Max Boxes with four extra ways to steer the carving.
situation: Box carving that has to respect something beyond geometry: a weight painted onto the Vtx, a shape budget that differs per axis, or a structural boundary the edges describe.

name: Decomposition Factory
purpose: The shared base of the decomposition rules that Cluster : Decomposition picks from.
situation: Reading any of the Decompose sub-nodes and needing to know what all seven guarantee about the grouping they hand back.

name: Decompose : Spectral
purpose: The one rule of the seven that decides on connectivity.
situation: Cutting a cluster where its structure is thin, so the pieces are held together by their own connections instead of by proximity.

name: Decompose : Threshold
purpose: Groups the Vtx by a number they already carry.
situation: A value already written onto the Vtx, a height or a density or a sampled field, that has to become discrete groups the rest of the graph can act on.

name: Default Actor Content Filter
purpose: Decides which actors in a level count when something reads that level.
situation: A level being read into a collection is full of gameplay volumes, spawn markers and helper actors that should not count toward what that level is.

name: Default Actor Mesh Classificator
purpose: Decides which actors a level export opens up.
situation: A level export came back with hand-placed scenery as actor references when those actors should have arrived as staged meshes.

name: Default Bounds Evaluator
purpose: Decides what counts as an actor's size when a staging rebuild measures one.
situation: An entry bakes bounds far larger than anything visible on the actor, and every point staged from it fits against the wrong box.

name: Default Level Data Exporter
purpose: The exporter that runs when a PCG Data Asset Collection captures a level and nothing else is assigned.
situation: A level was dressed by hand, and the capture has to keep its meshes, its configured actors and its nested level instances apart.

name: Destroy Actor
purpose: Destroys named actors, but only ones the PCG component running this graph spawned itself.
situation: Spawned actors that have to go before the rest of a generation continues, selected by a reference list the graph has already built.

name: Discard By Overlap
purpose: Resolves conflicts between whole datasets by throwing some of them away.
situation: Several candidate layouts scattered over the same ground, where only the ones that do not fight each other should survive.

name: Discard By Point Count
purpose: Splits datasets by how many points they hold.
situation: A pin carrying many datasets of wildly different sizes, where the small ones, the huge ones, or both are noise for what comes next.

name: Discard Same
purpose: Finds datasets that are duplicates of each other and routes all but one of each family to Discarded.
situation: A pin carrying datasets that several upstream branches produced independently, where the same shape has arrived more than once.

name: Dispatch Subgraphs
purpose: Runs a subgraph chosen by the data rather than by the wiring.
situation: A table of work where each row names which graph should process it and with what settings, and the set of graphs is not known when the parent graph is authored.

name: Filter : Distance
purpose: Answers how close each element sits to a set of reference points, and turns that into a pass or fail.
situation: A second point set is on hand, and whether an element survives depends on how near it sits to that set.

name: Tuple : Distribute
purpose: Hands each point one whole row of a table authored on the node.
situation: Several attributes have to vary together in fixed combinations, and each point should receive one whole combination.

name: Filter : Dot
purpose: Compares two directions per element and turns how closely they agree into a pass or fail.
situation: A direction is already on the elements, and what survives depends on how closely it agrees with another direction.

name: Draw Attributes
purpose: Draws attribute values in the viewport so they can be looked at rather than inferred.
situation: A graph producing the wrong result for a reason that would be obvious if the intermediate values could be seen.

name: Dynamic Mesh to Clusters
purpose: Reads dynamic mesh data off a wire and hands back its topology as a cluster, one per input mesh.
situation: A dynamic mesh built earlier in the graph carries the connectivity wanted, and the next step needs it as cluster data.

name: Edge Filter : Endpoints Check
purpose: Turns a condition about Vtx into a condition about edges.
situation: A condition that is natural to write about a Vtx, and the node downstream takes edges.

name: Edge Filter : Endpoints Compare (Numeric)
purpose: Judges an edge by the numbers sitting on the two Vtx it connects.
situation: A value written per Vtx, and the edges worth keeping are the ones whose two ends disagree about it in one particular direction.

name: Edge Filter : Endpoints Compare (String)
purpose: Judges an edge by the text on the two Vtx it connects.
situation: Names or tags written per Vtx, and the edges worth keeping are the ones whose two ends match, differ, or nest one inside the other.

name: Edge Filter : Endpoints Regex
purpose: Tests the text on each of an edge's two Vtx against one pattern, then folds the two answers into a single verdict for the edge.
situation: Names or tags written per Vtx with a family structure in them, and the edges worth keeping are the ones whose ends belong to that family.

name: Score-based refinements
purpose: Four rules that rank the edges at each Vtx by heuristic score and act on the single best or worst one.
situation: Reach for these when the cluster carries a cost you already trust and you want one edge per Vtx chosen by it, rather than a global structure like a spanning tree.

name: Length-based refinements
purpose: Four rules that rank the edges at each Vtx by length and act on the single shortest or longest one.
situation: **Keep Shortest** is the one to reach for first. What comes out is a nearest-neighbour structure: every Vtx joined to whichever Vtx is closest to it, plus whatever its neighbours reached for.

name: Edge Filter : Length
purpose: Judges an edge by how long it is.
situation: A cluster built by a proximity or triangulation node, where the long connections it produced are the ones to drop.

name: Edge Filter : Num Vtx
purpose: Judges an edge by how connected its two ends are.
situation: A cluster where the edges hanging off dead ends should be treated differently from the ones between busy junctions.

name: Cluster : Edge Order
purpose: Decides, once and for the whole cluster, which endpoint of every edge is its start.
situation: A cluster is about to feed something that treats an edge as going somewhere, and the edges came from a generator that had no opinion about which way.

name: Refine : Filter
purpose: Hands the keep-or-cut decision to a filter stack.
situation: A cluster has to be thinned by a condition you author about the edges themselves rather than by geometry, length or score.

name: Refine : Chain Filter
purpose: Judges whole runs of edges instead of single edges.
situation: A cluster has grown stubs and detours that only read as wrong at the scale of a whole run, so cutting edge by edge would leave the fragments behind.

name: Refine : Gabriel
purpose: Keeps an edge only when nothing else stands between its two Vtx.
situation: A Delaunay or probe-built cluster connects points that have something closer sitting between them, and only the direct neighbours should stay joined.

name: Refine Operation
purpose: The base every refinement inherits, and the page carrying what all eighteen of them have in common.
situation: Reading any refinement page and needing to know what its rule is handed, what it is allowed to change, and why the node around it looks different from one rule to the next.

name: Refine : Line Trace
purpose: The one rule that looks at the level.
situation: A cluster generated over a floor plan connects rooms straight through the walls between them.

name: Refine : MST (Prim)
purpose: Cuts a cluster down to the cheapest tree that still reaches every Vtx.
situation: A dense cluster has to become a road, pipe or cable network that reaches everything once and doubles back nowhere.

name: Refine : β Skeleton
purpose: Removes an edge when another Vtx crowds the space beside it, with one number deciding how much space that is.
situation: A cluster needs thinning by proximity, and the fixed Gabriel test either cuts too much or leaves too much.

name: Refine : DFS (Tarjan)
purpose: Finds the edges that hold the cluster together, and by default takes them out.
situation: A generator produced a tangle of loops joined by single-edge tethers, and only the loops are wanted.

name: Remove Leaves
purpose: Cuts the dead ends off a cluster in one sweep.
situation: A generated cluster has grown spurs off its junctions and only the connected body is wanted.

name: Remove Leaves (Recursive)
purpose: Strips the dead ends off a cluster, then the dead ends that leaves behind, and keeps going.
situation: A cluster is meant to be all loops, and the generator left branching debris hanging off it.

name: Refine : Overlap
purpose: Removes edges that cross or run too close to another edge.
situation: Probes connected the same neighbourhood from several directions and the result is full of edges crossing over each other.

name: Data Filter : Entry Count
purpose: Compares how many points a dataset holds against a number, and answers for the dataset as a whole.
situation: A pin carrying datasets of wildly different sizes, where the small ones are noise and should be dropped before the expensive work starts.

name: Path : Extrude
purpose: Grows a path past one or both of its ends, adding a new tip and, if asked, the points between the old end and that tip.
situation: A path stops short of where it needs to reach, and the continuation has to leave from its existing end rather than replace it.

name: Tensors : Extrude
purpose: Turns points into paths by walking them through a tensor field: each seed asks the field which way to go, takes a step, and asks again, leaving a trail behind it.
situation: A field has been authored and something has to follow it: streamlines, growth from a set of starting points, or routes that stop when they meet each other.

name: Factory : Provider
purpose: The base every sub-node inherits.
situation: Reading any of the sub-node pages and needing to know what a factory pin means and how several on one pin combine.

name: Fill Control : Attribute Accumulation
purpose: Adds an attribute up along a lane and stops the lane when the total passes a ceiling.
situation: The fill should get further through cheap ground than expensive, with cost already written on the cluster rather than expressed as heuristics.

name: Fill Control : Attribute Threshold
purpose: Reads one number off the Vtx or the edge in front of the fill and compares it against a threshold.
situation: A single attribute already marks where the fill should stop, and a filter stack is more machinery than one comparison needs.

name: Fill Control : Branch Limit
purpose: Caps how often a fill forks.
situation: A root, river or crack pattern is wanted and the raw fill covers everything instead of running in lanes.

name: Fill Control : Count
purpose: Caps how many Vtx one diffusion may hold.
situation: Several seeds have to claim territories of comparable size regardless of how dense the cluster happens to be around each of them.

name: Fill Control : Depth
purpose: Stops a diffusion at a set number of hops from its seed.
situation: A spread has to reach a fixed number of connections out from each seed however far apart the Vtx happen to sit.

name: Fill Control : Edge Filters
purpose: Puts a filter stack on the connections rather than on the Vtx: an edge that fails cannot be crossed.
situation: The fill has to be held back at a boundary that lives on the edges rather than on the Vtx.

name: Fill Controls Definition
purpose: The base every Fill Control : node inherits.
situation: Reading any fill control page and needing to know what Steps and Source do to it, or why a control that looks configured is having no effect.

name: Fill Control : Heuristics Budget
purpose: A spending limit on a lane.
situation: A spread should cover a lot of easy ground and little difficult ground, with difficulty already described by heuristics.

name: Fill Control : Heuristics Scoring
purpose: The bridge between heuristics and a fill.
situation: A fill should run down the cheap routes first, with cheap meaning the same thing it means to the pathfinding nodes.

name: Fill Control : Heuristics Threshold
purpose: A limit on one step rather than on a lane's total.
situation: A spread must not cross anything the heuristics call expensive, however much cheap ground it has covered getting there.

name: Fill Control : Keep Direction
purpose: Keeps a lane going the way it was already going.
situation: A fill through a dense cluster comes out as a stain, and what was wanted was a few lanes that hold a heading.

name: Fill Control : Length
purpose: Stops a diffusion on distance.
situation: A spread has to reach a fixed distance from each seed rather than a fixed number of connections.

name: Fill Control : Running Average
purpose: Keeps a lane on values close to the ones behind it.
situation: A spread should follow ground of a consistent height, density or any other single value rather than taking whatever is adjacent.

name: Fill Control : Vtx Filters
purpose: Puts a filter stack in the way of the fill: a Vtx that fails is not taken.
situation: A fill has to stay inside a region, or out of one, and the boundary is something a filter can already tell about a Vtx.

name: Point Filter Definition
purpose: Every filter node emits one factory, and this is the contract the seventy-odd consumers read it through.
situation: Working out why a filter that looks right in the details panel is refused, ignored, or quietly replaced by a constant on the pin it was wired into.

name: Filter Group
purpose: Several filters landing on one pin already mean AND.
situation: A condition that is not a plain AND of everything on the pin: an either-or, or a whole set of tests inverted together.

name: Filter : Abstract
purpose: Every filter node except Filter Group inherits this base, and this page carries the settings they all share: the Priority that orders a stack before it runs, and the Warnings and Errors policies deciding what a filter does when it cannot do its job.
situation: Reading any filter page and needing to know what its `Priority`, `Initialization Failure Policy` or `Missing Data Policy` does, since those three are the same on every filter node.

name: Cluster : Filter Vtx
purpose: Removes Vtx from a cluster by a condition you author.
situation: A cluster was generated across a whole site, and everything outside a volume, below a slope, or missing an attribute has to come out of it.

name: Pathfinding : Find All Cells (Bounded)
purpose: Pathfinding : Find All Cells with the result sorted by how each cell sits against a box.
situation: A decomposition running past the edge of the area being built, where the cells that hang over it have to be told apart from the ones fully inside.

name: Pathfinding : Find All Cells
purpose: The whole decomposition at once: every region the cluster's edges enclose, without anything having to point at them.
situation: A planar cluster whose faces are the point of it, and every one of them is wanted.

name: Pathfinding : Find Cluster Hull
purpose: The outer boundary of a cluster rather than anything enclosed inside it.
situation: The silhouette of a cluster is wanted as a path, to inset, offset, or test something against.

name: Find Clusters
purpose: Sorts a mixed pile of datasets into cluster pairs and hands each half out on its own pin.
situation: Both halves of a cluster travelled through one reroute, or a loop is walking Edges datasets and each pass needs the Vtx that goes with it.

name: Pathfinding : Find Cells (Bounded)
purpose: Pathfinding : Find Cells with the cells the seeds claimed sorted by how each one sits against a box.
situation: Seeded regions near the edge of a working area, where the ones that spill past it have to be handled differently from the ones that do not.

name: Pathfinding : Find Cells
purpose: Takes the cell around each seed you hand it, and nothing else.
situation: A cluster whose interior regions matter one at a time, and points already sitting in the ones that matter.

name: Cluster : Find point on Bounds
purpose: Reduces each cluster to a single point: the Vtx, or the point on an edge, nearest a spot you choose on that cluster's own bounding box.
situation: Every cluster in a batch needs one marker, and it has to sit on the same side of each of them.

name: Find point on Bounds
purpose: Finds the point in a dataset that sits nearest a chosen spot on the dataset's own bounds.
situation: A scatter that needs a representative at a known corner or face, chosen from the points that are actually there.

name: Abstract Fitting
purpose: The shared half of the fitting relaxations: Box Fitting, Box Fitting v2 and Radius Fitting.
situation: Reading Box Fitting, Box Fitting v2 or Radius Fitting and needing to know what the four settings they all have in common actually do.

name: Cluster : Write States
purpose: Turns a stack of named conditions into one number on every Vtx.
situation: A cluster whose Vtx have to be classified once, several ways at a time, so everything downstream can select on the classification instead of recomputing it.

name: Flat Projection
purpose: Flattens points onto a plane, and can put them back afterwards.
situation: Work that only makes sense in plan view, on points that still need their original heights when it is done.

name: Flatten
purpose: Hands back a copy of each input that owns every attribute it carries, with no reference back to the data it came from.
situation: Data another PCG component will read across the component boundary, most often the output of a graph that Wait for PCG Data is watching.

name: Force Directed
purpose: Spreads a cluster out under two competing forces, one pulling along the edges and one pushing everything apart.
situation: A cluster generated somewhere the positions were incidental, where what the layout should show is which Vtx connect to which.

name: Format Attributes
purpose: String templating over attributes: name a literal token, point it at another attribute, and every occurrence of that token inside the chosen FName and FString attributes becomes that attribute's value.
situation: A name or path attribute has to be assembled per row from values that live in other attributes.

name: From Neighbors
purpose: Builds each point's tangent from the two runs leading away from it, one back to the previous point and one on to the next, averaged at half weight.
situation: A path is on its way to a spline and needs an even, neighbour-driven tangent at every interior point.

name: From Transform
purpose: The one rule that ignores the path: each point's tangent comes from its own rotation, so order and spacing change nothing.
situation: Point rotations already carry the direction the curve should take, and the tangents should follow them rather than the point positions.

name: Cluster : Fuse
purpose: Merges every cluster on its inputs into one, welding Vtx that land in the same place and optionally resolving the places where the geometry meets without sharing a point.
situation: Modular cluster pieces, or a pathfinding result converted back, have to become one network at the seams where they overlap.

name: Path : Fuse Collinear
purpose: Drops the points that were not doing anything.
situation: A path that came out of an operation with far more points than its shape needs, a boolean result or a dense conversion being the usual sources.

name: Fuse Points
purpose: Merges points that sit close enough together into one.
situation: Points arriving from several sources that land near enough to each other to be the same thing, and should be treated as one.

name: Filter : GameplayTags
purpose: Answers a question about an actor in the level rather than about the element in front of it.
situation: Points were built from actors already placed in the level, and which of them the next node touches depends on the tags those actors carry.

name: Get Collection Data
purpose: Turns a collection into rows.
situation: A collection has to be read out as subdivision modules, or a module that resolved to a sub-collection has to be opened one level further.

name: Get GUID
purpose: Reads the identity of one point instead of stamping every point with its own.
situation: One value out of a dataset that has to seed or key something else in the graph, taken from a known position rather than from every point.

name: Get Path Data
purpose: Reads spline components straight off selected actors and hands back a path per component, with the actor it came from recorded on the data.
situation: Splines authored on level actors have to become paths, and something further down still needs to know which actor each one belongs to.

name: Get Properties Data
purpose: Turns actor references into attributes.
situation: Points or rows carrying actor references, where the decisions downstream depend on values authored on those actors rather than on anything the graph knows.

name: Get Sketch Data
purpose: Reads PCGEx Cluster Sketch components off actors and prints each one as a cluster, placed by the component's world transform, so the output matches 1:1 what is authored and visible in the level.
situation: Sketches were authored on actors in the level, and a graph needs them as clusters exactly where they sit.

name: Get Texture Data
purpose: Turns asset paths carried on points into texture data something can sample.
situation: Points that know which material or texture they belong to, and a graph that needs to read pixels out of it.

name: Get Zone Graph Constants
purpose: Lists what the project's Zone Graph settings actually define, as data.
situation: A graph choosing a lane profile or tag, where the names should come from the project rather than being typed.

name: Goal Picker : Default
purpose: The base every goal picker inherits, and the choice a node starts on.
situation: Seeds and goals arrive as two datasets whose rows already correspond, and each seed should route to the goal on its own row.

name: Goal Picker : All
purpose: Every seed routes to every goal.
situation: The routes between two sets of points are all wanted, not just one pairing of them.

name: Goal Picker : Index Attribute
purpose: Each seed names its own goal, by reading a row index out of an attribute it carries.
situation: Which goal a seed should reach was already worked out by earlier nodes and written onto the seed.

name: Goal Picker : Random
purpose: Each seed draws its goals at random.
situation: Routes are wanted between two sets of points without any particular pairing, only coverage.

name: Grammar Node Settings
purpose: Every node in a grammar graph carries these, whatever it does.
situation: Reading the fields above a grammar node own settings, whichever node it is.

name: Grammar Growth
purpose: Replaces the growth strategy with a Structural Grammar: an authored graph that says what to place, in what order, and under what conditions.
situation: The structure has a recipe, and expressing that recipe as connector rules and a frontier ordering would be indirect at best.

name: Placing Node Settings
purpose: What a node that places modules carries on top of the shared node settings.
situation: Attaching a rule or a property value to one node rather than to a whole region.

name: Heuristics : Feedback
purpose: Charges for traffic.
situation: Several routes across one cluster should not end up on top of each other.

name: Heuristics : Azimuth
purpose: Measures heading.
situation: A route wanders sideways across a dense cluster because every local edge is short, and what it needs is a sense of which way the destination lies.

name: Heuristics Definition
purpose: The base every Heuristics : node inherits.
situation: Reading any heuristic page and needing to know what Weight Factor and Invert do to its number, or what happens to three of them wired onto one pin.

name: Heuristics : Gradient
purpose: Charges for how much a Vtx attribute changes across a step, and in which direction.
situation: A value is painted across the Vtx and a route should follow its slope rather than its level.

name: Heuristics : Inertia
